memory_update.text: AXTI should remain in the CPO/silicon-photonics manufacturing-stack universe as an underfollowed InP substrate candidate; main verification issues are export permits, actual AI/datacenter customer exposure, substrate diameter mix, and backlog quality.

VECO should remain in the universe as a compound-semiconductor/photonics equipment candidate; evidence is strong for photonics and MOCVD exposure but still needs direct order-level confirmation tied to InP lasers, optical engines, or CPO ramps.
FORM is a relatively clean underfollowed test-capacity candidate because it explicitly markets wafer-level silicon-photonics test systems for AI, CPO, and data-center production.

The node should be tracked as a multi-bottleneck stack: InP substrates, MOCVD/epitaxy equipment, bonding/process yield, and wafer-level optical test may each gate CPO commercialization at different production phases.

Need a later pass on non-US primary listings and ADR/OTC names such as Aixtron, Oxford Instruments, Huber+Suhner, Sumitomo Electric, Disco, Advantest, and Tokyo Electron because several key upstream chokepoints are not cleanly captured by US-listed equities.

node: CPO and silicon-photonics upstream manufacturing stack: InP substrates, epitaxy, MOCVD, etch/deposition, bonding, optical test
summary: Layer 1B expansion focused on US-listed companies with direct or second-order exposure to the upstream manufacturing constraints behind CPO and silicon photonics. The discovery lane emphasizes InP substrates, compound-semiconductor deposition/etch, and wafer-level optical test rather than obvious switch ASIC or hyperscaler demand owners. The strongest underfollowed candidates in this pass are AXTI for InP substrates, VECO for compound-semiconductor/photonics process equipment, and FORM for wafer-level silicon-photonics optical test automation. COHR is included as a high-attention reference anchor because it connects the InP and AI optical transceiver demand signal to downstream datacenter deployment.
